The compound is identified as a target of two different molecules: cis-Isopinocamphone and (1S,4R,7R)-5-methyl-7-[(2S)-6-methylhept-5-en-2-yl]-2,3-dioxabicyclo[2.2.2]oct-5-ene. Both of these molecules are known to interact with the DNMT3A2/3L complex, indicating a possible pathway through which the compound may exert its effects. The evidence suggests that the compound may act as a modulator of the DNMT3A2/3L complex, potentially influencing DNA methylation processes. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the scores are relatively low, but the cumulative evidence from multiple paths supports a plausible mechanism of action. The exact nature of the interaction remains uncertain, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the role of this compound in DNMT3A2/3L complex regulation.
